sentences.text:
Brief facts of prosecution case is as follows:
On 13.01.2019 at 3.30p.m., the accused without obtaining license, illegally, by endangering human life, without providing safety measure was getting filled LPG gas to small cylinders from big cylinders at a shed, which is situated adjacent to Kukkadeshwari Nilaya, 5th cross, Varadaraju layout main road, Amruthahalli and as such, due to his negligence, the cylinder got burst and CW.1 and 2 sustained burn injuries.
On the basis of statement given by CW.1 before the medical officer of Axis hospital, the Amruthahalli Police have registered this case against the accused in Cr.No.11/2019.
3. On 14.01.2019, the accused was arrested and produced before the Court.
On the same day, the Court enlarged him on bail.
4. After the investigation, the IO filed charge sheet against the accused.
The Court has taken cognizance of the offences punishable U/Sec. for the O/P/U/Sec. 285, 337 of IPC, Sec.3, 4, 5, 7 of LPG orders and Sec.3 and 7 of Essential Commodities Act.
The Court complied with Sec.207 of Cr.P.C., and furnished charge sheet copy to the accused.
5. The Court framed accusation for the offences punishable U/Sec. 285, 337 of IPC, Sec.3, 4, 5, 7 of LPG orders and Sec.3 and 7 of Essential Commodities Act and recorded the plea of the accused.
The accused did not plead guilty.
He claimed to be tried.
6. In order to prove its case, the prosecution got examined 5 witnesses as PW.1 to 5 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 6 documents.
After the closure of the evidence of the prosecution, this court recorded the statement of the accused U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C., wherein, he denied the incriminating evidence led against him.
He did not choose to lead his defense evidence.
7. I have heard the arguments of Senior APP and Sri.LRY Advocate.

8. On the basis of allegations made against the accused, the following points arise for my consideration:
1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused by endangering human life, without providing safety measures was getting filled LPG gas to small cylinders from big cylinders on 13.01.2019 at 3.30p.m., at a shed, which is situated adjacent to Kukkadeshwari Nilaya, 5th cross, Varadaraju layout main road, Amruthahalli and thereby he has committed the offence punishable U/Sec.285 of IPC?
2.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the aforesaid date, time and place, due to the negligence of the accused, the gas cylinder got burst and CW.1 and 2 sustained burn injuries and thereby he has committed the offence punishable U/Sec.337 of IPC?

sentences.text: Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the aforesaid date, time and place the accused without obtaining license, illegally getting filled LPG gas to small cylinders from big cylinders and thereby he has committed the offence punishable U/Sec.3, 4, 5, 7 of LPG orders and Sec.3 and 7 of Essential Commodities Act?
4. What order?

9. My answers to the above points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In Negative  Point No.2 : In Negative  Point No.3 : In Negative  Point No.4 : As per final orders for the following:
 REASONS Point No.1 to 3:As these three points are interrelated, I take all the three points together for common discussion to avoid repetition.
10. The burden is casted on the prosecution to prove that, the accused without obtaining license,
illegally, by endangering human life, without providing safety measures was getting filled LPG gas to small cylinders from big cylinders on 13.01.2019 at 3.30p.m., at a shed, which is situated adjacent to Kukkadeshwari Nilaya, 5th cross, Varadaraju layout main road, Amruthahalli and due to his negligence, the gas cylinder got burst and CW.1 and 2 sustained burn injuries.
11.

In order to prove its case, the prosecution got examined the eye witness/CW.4 as PW.1, mahazer witnesses/CW.7 as PW.4, CW.8 as PW.5, the officer who registered the case/CW.10 as PW.2 and treated doctor/CW.9 as PW.3 and got marked portion of the statement of PW.1 as Ex.P.1, statement cum complaint as Ex.P.2, FIR as Ex.P.3 and wound certificates as Ex.P.4 and 5 respectively.

12 . CW.10/PW.2-S.Jayananda in his evidence has stated that, when he was working as PSI at Amruthahalli police station on 13.01.2019 at 6.30 p.m., he visited Axis hospital, Jakkur and recorded Ex.P.2/statement of CW.1 in the presence of doctor, who was taking treatment therein and registered Ex.P.3/FIR.
13.

CW.9/PW.3-Dr.Kiran, in his evidence has stated that, while he was working as medical officer at Axis Hospital, Amruthahalli, on 13.01.2019 at 5p.m., one Vittal brought CW.1 and 2 to their hospital for treatment with the history of cylinder blast.

On examination he noticed 18% burn injuries over both upper limbs and left foot of CW.2 and CW.1 had sustained 1st and 2nd degree of burn injuries on the face to an extent of 6% and hairs of scalp was burnt.
Those injuries were fresh and simple in nature.
Accordingly, he issued Ex.P.4 and 5 wound certificates.
Such injuries can be sustained due to cylinder blast, while refilling the cylinders.
14. CW.4/PW.1-Suresh in his evidence has stated that, he is not acquainted with the accused and CW.1 to 3.
He does not know anything about this case.
The police did not enquire him.

He has not Santhosh vs Vittal Rao.L on 30 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65966936/
3 given any statement to the police.
15. CW.7/PW.4-Raju in his evidence has stated that, he has seen the accused earlier.
Ex .P.6 mahazer bears his signature.
He signed that document near his shop.
But, he does not remember, when he signed the same.
The police neither taken him to any place nor taken any action in his presence.
16. CW.8/PW.5-Chiranjeevi in his evidence has stated that, he has seen the accused earlier.
Ex . P.6 mahazer bears his signature.
About 4-5 years ago, he signed that document near his shop.
The police neither taken him to any place nor taken any action in his presence.

17. On the basis of Ex.P.2 statement given by CW.1 before the doctor of Axis Hospital, Amruthahalli on 13.01.2019 at 6.30p.m., the Amruthahalli police have registered this case, investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the accused.

In Ex.P.1, the CW.1 had mentioned the name of the accused, who was doing gas refilling work on 13.01.2019 at 3.30p.m., at a shed, which is situated adjacent to Kukkadeshwari Nilaya, 5th cross, Varadaraju layout main road, Amruthahalli and due to his negligence, the gas cylinder got burst and he along with Anji sustained burn injuries.
18.
In order to ascertain the correctness of the allegations made in Ex.P.2, this Court had issued repeated summons, non-bailable warrants and proclamations against CW.1 to 3, 5, 6 and 11.
On 25.07.2024 and 26.07.2024, the police published proclamation against CW.1, 2 and 5.

Inspite of it,
they did not appear before the Court.
Likewise, the CW.3 and 6 did not appear before the Court.
The CW.11 being the IO did not care to appear before the Court to give his evidence to explain the manner in which he conducted investigation of this case.
By noting the absence of the witnesses and age of the case, this Court dropped them from examination.
19. The CW.1 and 2 did not appear before the Court to explain how they sustained burn injuries on 13.01.2019 and the hospital, where they had taken treatment.
The PW.1 being an eye witness to the alleged incident, did not depose in support of the case of the prosecution.
He has gone to the extent of saying that he does not know anything about this case.
He denied that CW.1 and 2 sustained burn injuries due to the negligence of the accused, when the cylinder got burst while refilling the same from big cylinders to small cylinders.

20. The PW.4 and 5 being the signatories to Ex.P.6 mahazer have denied that, the police have inspected the shed, which is situated adjacent to Kukkadeshwari Nilaya, 5th cross, Varadaraju layout main road, Amruthahalli on 14.01.2019 at 8.45a.m, in their presence, where the gas cylinder got burst and they seized the instruments which were used for refilling the gas, by drawing Ex.P.6.
21 . As per the endorsement made on Ex.P.2, the PW.2 allegedly recorded the statement of CW.1 at Axis hospital, Amruthahalli in the presence of Dr.Amarnath.K.A.
But, that doctor is not arrayed as witness to this case.
The PW.2 deposed regarding recording of statement of CW.1 at Axis hospital and registration of this case.
However, his version is not supported by the oral evidence of injured/complainant or doctor, in whose presence the PW.2 allegedly recorded Ex.P.2 statement.

4 22.
According to PW.3, one Vittal brought CW.1 and 2 to Axis hospital for treatment for the injuries sustained in cylinder blast.
But, that Vittal has not been arrayed as witness to this case.
The PW.3 deposed regarding the nature of injuries sustained by CW.1 and 2 and its history.
But, in the present case, the CW.1 and 2 being the injured did not appear before the Court to substantiate the version of PW.3 and the contents of Ex.P.4 and 5.
In the absence of oral evidence of CW.1 and 2, the evidence led by PW.3 appears to be baseless.

23. In the present case, no single witness appeared before the Court to say that, the accused illegally,
by endangering human life was refilling gas cylinders on 13.01.2019 at 3.30p.m., at a shed, which is situated adjacent to Kukkadeshwari Nilaya, 5th cross, Varadaraju layout main road, Amruthahalli and due to his negligence, the gas cylinder got burst and CW.1 and 2 sustained burn injuries.
24.
From the evidence led by PW.1 to 5, the charges levelled against the accused are not proved.
There is no convincing evidence to connect the accused with the alleged crime.

Though there are wound certificates before the Court to hold that, the CW.1 and 2 sustained burn injuries, there is no material before the Court to hold that, they sustained injuries due to the negligence of the accused.
25.

Thus, the prosecution has failed to prove that, the accused without obtaining license, illegally,by endangering human life, without providing safety measures was getting filled LPG gas to small cylinders from big cylinders on 13.01.2019 at 3.30p.m., at a shed, which is situated adjacent to Kukkadeshwari Nilaya, 5th cross, Varadaraju layout main road, Amruthahalli and due to his negligence, the gas cylinder got burst and CW.1 and 2 sustained burn injuries.
In such circumstances, I answer point No.1 to 3 in Negative.
Point No.4:

For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

By exercising the powers conferred U/Sec.255[1] of Cr.P.C., the accused is acquitted from the charges of Sec. 285, 337 of IPC, Sec.3, 4, 5, 7 of LPG orders and Sec.3 and 7 of Essential Commodities Act.
Bail bonds executed by the accused stands cancelled.
Bonds executed by the accused U/Sec.437[A] of Cr.P.C., will be in force for a period of 6 months.
The property seized under PF No.9/2019 i.e., cylinders, weighing machine and refilling rods are ordered to be handed over to the department of food and civil supplies.
